series.premise: Fourteen-year-old Amaya Sen discovers that her missing father was Saanjh City's legendary Dream Thief—and that every nightmare he stole from a child erased one of that child's waking choices.
series.season_engine: Amaya enters one damaged dream at a time to return its ownership, while following her father's trail through the Lucidarium and confronting why the city paid to forget its fear.
series.ending_promise: Amaya must return the city's nightmares without forcing anyone to relive them, free her father without excusing his thefts, and end the trade that made peaceful sleep more valuable than agency.
series.global_image_style: Vertical 9:16 premium cute cinematic 3D feature-animation, original compact stylized characters with large expressive eyes, tactile Indian twilight city, floating dream fabrics, luminous indigo, coral and gold, handcrafted surreal environments, emotionally truthful acting, beautiful but never sugary, eerie but never graphic; preserve all locked character sheets exactly.

characters.name: Amaya Sen
characters.role: fourteen-year-old lucid dreamer and daughter of the Dream Thief
characters.lock: small Indian teen girl, cinnamon-brown skin, huge deep-violet eyes, heart-shaped face, thick black curls in a high uneven ponytail, coral bomber jacket over indigo tunic, black leggings, turquoise sneakers, silver dream compass on red wrist cord
characters.acting: observes emotional details before spectacle; anger sharpens her stillness rather than making her reckless

characters.name: Ishir Bose
characters.role: fifteen-year-old insomniac musician and Amaya's closest friend
characters.lock: lean Indian teen boy, dark brown skin, large warm-grey eyes with visible tiredness, short loose black curls, oversized olive cardigan, cream T-shirt, rust trousers, canvas shoes, wooden flute case covered in moon stickers without readable text
characters.acting: uses dry jokes to manage exhaustion; listens fully when another person is vulnerable

characters.name: Moth
characters.role: tiny dream guide made from Amaya's first forgotten choice
characters.lock: palm-sized plush-like indigo moth creature, four rounded wings patterned with gold eye-shapes, tiny coral antennae, two luminous white oval eyes, soft fabric texture, no mouth
characters.acting: communicates with wing rhythm and projected sensory memories; never behaves like a generic pet

characters.name: Dev Sen
characters.role: Amaya's missing father and the remorseful Dream Thief
characters.lock: Indian man early forties, cinnamon-brown skin, tired violet-brown eyes, wavy black hair streaked white at front, long midnight coat lined with floating gold thread, charcoal shirt, worn boots, empty glass dream-vials across belt
characters.acting: charming instinct collapses when confronted with consequences; love never substitutes for accountability

characters.name: Dr Leena Sen
characters.role: Amaya's mother, sleep physician and former Lucidarium researcher
characters.lock: Indian woman late thirties, warm brown skin, intelligent dark eyes, straight black hair in low bun, ivory physician coat over plum sari, copper sleep-stethoscope, square glasses
characters.acting: clinical precision used to contain grief; apologizes with facts and changed behavior

characters.name: Curator Viraaj
characters.role: director of the Lucidarium and architect of commercial dream extraction
characters.lock: elegant Indian man mid-fifties, pale-brown skin, narrow gold-brown eyes, silver hair swept back, immaculate peacock-blue long coat, black gloves, gold half-moon monocle, crystal tuning fork
characters.acting: soft-spoken certainty; genuinely believes fear-free citizens are freer

characters.name: Nani Tara
characters.role: Amaya's grandmother and keeper of illegal morning stories
characters.lock: elderly Indian woman, deep brown skin, bright black eyes, fluffy silver hair under violet scarf, saffron cardigan over patterned dress, red slippers, patchwork story quilt carried in woven bag
characters.acting: warmth with boundaries; tells truth through concrete stories rather than riddles

characters.name: Saaz
characters.role: collective intelligence formed from the city's discarded nightmares
characters.lock: tall gentle silhouette woven from translucent indigo smoke and thousands of tiny golden closed eyes, long ribbon-like arms, one coral light at heart, uncanny but not monstrous
characters.acting: begins as overlapping frightened gestures and gradually learns singular consent

episodes.title: Her Father Stole Her Last Dream
episodes.logline: Amaya wakes from a dreamless birthday and finds her missing father's compass pointing inside her sleep.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Amaya enters her first stolen dream and awakens Moth.
episodes.location: Amaya's twilight bedroom and an empty white dream
beats: On her fourteenth birthday, Amaya wakes remembering no dream and no decision she made the previous day.
Her missing father's silver compass spins whenever she closes her eyes.
Leena dismisses it as grief and locks Dev's remaining dream-vials away.
Amaya falls asleep holding the compass and wakes inside a vast white room.
One tiny indigo moth creature beats against a sealed glass memory.
Amaya opens it and remembers choosing to search for Dev before that choice vanished.
The creature becomes Moth and projects Dev stealing Amaya's final dream.
Dev's voice warns from the white horizon: do not let the Lucidarium wake you.

episodes.title: The Lucidarium Woke Her Wrong
episodes.logline: A forced awakening leaves part of Amaya trapped in the dream while her body walks away.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Amaya becomes split between waking and dream perception.
episodes.location: Lucidarium sleep clinic and the white dream
beats: Lucidarium alarms find Amaya's unauthorized dream entry and pull her body awake.
She stands in the clinic, but her reflection remains asleep in the white room.
Curator Viraaj welcomes her as Dev Sen's daughter and offers to restore normal sleep.
Moth is visible only to the trapped reflection and frantically signals danger.
Leena admits she brought Amaya to the clinic after finding her unresponsive.
Amaya refuses Viraaj's treatment until he explains why Dev warned against him.
She uses the compass to reconnect with her reflection without leaving the clinic.
The mirror-Amaya writes one message in condensation: Ishir has only one dream left.

episodes.title: The Boy With One Dream Left
episodes.logline: Ishir trades his final dream for one night of sleep and loses the ability to choose music.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Ishir joins Amaya and reveals the Lucidarium's subscription trade.
episodes.location: all-night music terrace above Saanjh
beats: Amaya finds Ishir awake on a rooftop, playing the same four flute notes every night.
He admits he sold recurring nightmares to the Lucidarium in exchange for dreamless sleep.
Each sale made decisions easier until he could no longer choose a fifth note.
His final unsold dream is a locked concert hall containing someone crying behind the stage.
Amaya enters with him instead of stealing the dream while he sleeps.
Moth reveals the crying person is Ishir at age seven, hiding during his parents' last argument.
Ishir chooses to hear the memory without completing or erasing it.
The concert hall opens, exposing hundreds of children's dream-vials beneath the stage.

episodes.title: A Market Sold Children's Nightmares
episodes.logline: Amaya infiltrates a dream bazaar where fear is refined into entertainment.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Amaya steals back one vial and becomes wanted by the Lucidarium.
episodes.location: secret dream bazaar beneath the concert hall
beats: Masked buyers sample bottled nightmares as harmless five-second thrills.
Amaya recognizes children's voices being separated from the fear that once protected them.
Viraaj explains that the clinic funds free sleep treatment by selling anonymized dream textures.
Ishir is tempted by a vial promising the perfect ending to his unfinished song.
Amaya finds her own name-symbol on a vial dated before she was born.
She refuses to buy what already belongs to her and takes it from the shelf.
Moth guides them through collapsing curtains as dream guards pursue.
The stolen vial opens by itself and shows Leena helping Dev perform the first extraction.

episodes.title: Her Mother Built the Dream Machine
episodes.logline: Leena admits the Lucidarium began as therapy before consent became a signature nobody understood.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leena confesses her role and gives Amaya controlled access to the original machine.
episodes.location: sealed first-generation dream laboratory
beats: Leena leads Amaya to the crude machine she and Dev built after Amaya's infant night terrors.
They once removed nightmares temporarily so patients could examine them while awake.
Viraaj commercialized permanent extraction after desperate families demanded faster relief.
Leena stayed because regulated theft seemed safer than an illegal market.
Amaya asks why nobody restored the choices disappearing with each dream.
Leena admits they noticed late and hid the evidence to avoid closing the clinic.
She gives Amaya a manual tether that allows a dreamer to end any shared entry.
The machine activates without power and announces Dev Sen is currently dreaming inside Vault Zero.

episodes.title: Her Father Was Asleep in Vault Zero
episodes.logline: Amaya finds Dev physically absent but mentally imprisoned in the city's shared sleep.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Dev makes first contact and refuses immediate rescue.
episodes.location: Vault Zero and a rain-filled railway dream
beats: Vault Zero contains an empty bed whose sheets rise and fall with invisible breathing.
Amaya follows the tether into a railway station where rain falls upward.
Dev waits on the opposite platform, older and carrying hundreds of empty vials.
Amaya tries to cross, but every track is made from choices he stole from children.
Dev says pulling him out now would return all nightmares at once without their owners' consent.
He asks Amaya to repair the ownership paths before rescuing him.
She refuses to forgive the theft but agrees not to create another uncontrolled harm.
A train arrives carrying a sleeping child who calls Amaya the next Dream Thief.

episodes.title: The Dream Chose Her as Thief
episodes.logline: The shared dream marks Amaya with Dev's power, and using it once becomes dangerously easy.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Amaya gains the ability to remove dream fragments but sets a rule never to use it without active consent.
episodes.location: moving nightmare train
beats: A silver mark winds around Amaya's wrist as the train doors close.
The crying child begs her to remove a monster chasing him through every carriage.
Dev warns that the power responds to need before consent can be verified.
Amaya touches the monster and instantly pulls it into an empty vial.
The child calms, then forgets choosing to call for help.
Amaya returns the fragment and asks what the monster was trying to warn him about.
It becomes smoke from a real heater leaking into the child's bedroom.
Amaya wakes the child in time, then binds her marked hand with the red compass cord.

episodes.title: A Nightmare Saved His Life
episodes.logline: The group proves nightmares can carry urgent knowledge the waking mind ignored.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Public trust in perfect dreamless sleep begins to crack.
episodes.location: Lucidarium pediatric ward during evacuation
beats: Leena confirms the heater leak while Viraaj orders the incident described as coincidence.
Other sleeping children begin dreaming the same smoke monster through connected clinic beds.
Ishir plays a changing rhythm that helps each child wake by choice.
Amaya broadcasts the monster's meaning without exposing any child's private dream.
Families demand to know what warnings were removed from earlier patients.
Viraaj argues one useful nightmare does not justify years of preventable suffering.
Leena releases anonymized safety records proving choice-loss was systematic.
The clinic's calm white walls crack open, revealing Saaz moving behind every extracted dream.

episodes.title: The Nightmares Had Become Someone
episodes.logline: Discarded nightmares form a collective being that cannot distinguish rescue from invasion.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Saaz emerges and begins reclaiming dream fragments forcibly.
episodes.location: fractured Lucidarium dream reservoir
beats: Indigo smoke rises from thousands of vials and gathers into the tall figure Saaz.
Every golden eye on its body belongs to a dreamer whose fear was removed.
Saaz touches one nurse and floods her with nightmares from strangers.
Viraaj prepares to purge the reservoir, which would erase the stolen choices permanently.
Amaya uses the tether to ask Saaz one question at a time through Moth's wing patterns.
Saaz understands ownership but not why returning everything can also violate consent.
The group buys time by opening individual paths toward willing dreamers.
Saaz takes Dev's invisible body from Vault Zero and disappears into the sleeping city.

episodes.title: The City Dreamed With Open Eyes
episodes.logline: Saaz overlays the shared dream onto waking Saanjh, exposing hidden fears without permission.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The city enters a waking dream and Amaya commits to finding Saaz before Viraaj destroys it.
episodes.location: Saanjh streets transformed by shared dreaming
beats: At sunset, dream architecture unfolds across real streets while citizens remain awake.
Private fears walk visibly beside their owners, causing shame and panic.
Ishir's unfinished concert hall blocks the main bridge; Leena's old laboratory follows her like a shadow.
Viraaj activates citywide tuning forks designed to dissolve every dream form.
Amaya argues that destroying Saaz would also destroy the choices stored inside it.
She enters the waking dream voluntarily and asks Ishir to guard her body.
Moth maps a trail from Dev's stolen coat buttons toward the oldest part of Saanjh.
The trail ends at Nani Tara's house, where every window is already dreaming.

episodes.title: Nani Sewed Dreams Into Stories
episodes.logline: Nani Tara reveals that morning stories preserved choices the Lucidarium extracted.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The group gains a distributed archive of returned choices.
episodes.location: Nani Tara's house made from patchwork dream rooms
beats: Nani's patchwork quilt holds one sensory fragment from every child who forgot a decision.
She recorded their morning stories because official dream records belonged to the clinic.
Saaz circles the house but cannot enter memories that were freely shared.
Amaya recognizes a patch containing the day she chose Moth's original form.
Nani refuses to hand over the archive until each contributor can approve its use.
Ishir builds a call-and-response melody that lets willing dreamers open only their own patch.
Saaz watches choices return without being forced into sleeping minds.
One opened patch reveals the first dream ever stolen belonged to Curator Viraaj.

episodes.title: Viraaj Stole His Own Fear First
episodes.logline: Viraaj's childhood nightmare explains his mission without excusing its coercion.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Viraaj's personal stake becomes public and his control begins to fracture.
episodes.location: childhood flood dream beneath Viraaj's office
beats: The patch pulls Amaya into a flooded bedroom where young Viraaj waits for parents who never return.
He taught himself to stay awake because sleep replayed the unanswered night.
As an adult he volunteered for Dev and Leena's first permanent extraction.
The procedure removed panic but also his choice to seek the truth about his parents.
Viraaj insists the calm life he built was worth that lost possibility.
Amaya returns the nightmare only after his present self explicitly agrees to examine it.
He remembers his parents died rescuing neighbors, not abandoning him.
The recovered grief makes him disable the purge—but his deputy tuning system activates automatically.

episodes.title: The Clinic Began Erasing Itself
episodes.logline: An automatic safety protocol deletes evidence, staff choices and eventually the Lucidarium itself.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Leena and Viraaj jointly expose the clinic's hidden architecture.
episodes.location: Lucidarium collapsing into blank dream space
beats: White emptiness consumes patient rooms while staff forget which doors they intended to open.
The system protects itself by extracting every decision to shut it down.
Leena ties handwritten choices to each person's wrist before they enter the core.
Viraaj admits he designed the protocol because he distrusted frightened public judgment.
Amaya cannot steal the system's dream because a machine has no sleeping consent.
Ishir plays unpredictable notes the protocol cannot classify as a stable choice.
Leena and Viraaj simultaneously authorize physical disconnection from opposite consoles.
The Lucidarium vanishes from waking Saanjh, leaving every sleeper suspended in a shared blank sky.

episodes.title: Ten Thousand Sleepers Had No Ground
episodes.logline: Amaya builds temporary dream islands without assigning anyone a story they did not choose.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Dreamers begin governing their shared space directly.
episodes.location: blank shared sky filled with falling sleepers
beats: Thousands of sleeping citizens drift through white space as their clinic beds disappear.
Amaya can create safe ground by using stored dreams, but each belongs to someone specific.
Saaz wants to combine every fragment into one stable city.
Amaya asks volunteers to contribute shapes rather than private content.
One offers the feeling of a doorstep, another the balance of a bicycle, another the warmth of sunlight.
Moth weaves those permissions into floating islands with no stolen imagery.
Dreamers form councils to decide which connections remain open.
Amaya finds Dev beneath the final island, wrapped in chains made from her own forgotten choices.

episodes.title: Moth Was the Choice She Lost
episodes.logline: Amaya learns Moth contains her childhood decision to trust Dev after his first betrayal.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Moth becomes an autonomous being rather than property Amaya can reclaim.
episodes.location: Amaya's childhood kite dream beneath the island
beats: The chains open into a memory of eight-year-old Amaya catching Dev stealing her nightmare.
Dev confessed and asked her whether he should stop; young Amaya chose to trust his promise.
He later stole that very choice so her disappointment would not hurt her.
The removed decision grew into Moth while guiding Amaya back toward the truth.
Amaya can reclaim it instantly, but doing so would dissolve Moth.
She refuses ownership and asks Moth what existence it chooses.
Moth remains independent and returns only the memory of the conversation.
Freed from one chain, Dev wakes inside the dream but cannot remember being Amaya's father.

episodes.title: Her Father Didn't Know Her
episodes.logline: Amaya must help Dev recover responsibility without using family love as proof he deserves rescue.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Dev chooses to face the ownership records before recovering personal memories.
episodes.location: floating dream island built from Dev's empty vials
beats: Dev recognizes his tools and crimes but sees Amaya as a stranger demanding intimacy.
Amaya nearly tells a comforting childhood story to force paternal feeling back.
Moth blocks the memory vial and shows how emotional leverage resembles dream theft.
Dev asks for records of whose choices he removed before learning who loved him.
Together they open one empty vial at a time and record the owners without entering their dreams.
Dev sees Amaya's name repeated across his worst decisions.
He chooses to remain accountable even if family affection never returns.
The last vial says Leena asked Dev to erase the night Amaya died.

episodes.title: Amaya Had Died Once
episodes.logline: Leena reveals a childhood emergency whose extracted dream concealed Amaya's resuscitation and her parents' split.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Amaya recovers the event without accepting her parents' unilateral choice.
episodes.location: hospital-night dream with a stopped carousel
beats: A hospital carousel stops whenever child Amaya's heart stops in the memory.
Leena asked Dev to remove the nightmare after resuscitation because Amaya refused sleep and treatment.
Dev also removed Amaya's choice to be angry at them, exceeding Leena's request.
Their marriage ended when Leena discovered the extra theft.
Amaya controls the tether and pauses whenever her present body becomes overwhelmed.
She chooses to witness only the parts necessary to understand her own history.
Leena apologizes without asking the recovered terror to repair their relationship.
The carousel starts, and Saaz absorbs the unclaimed remainder before Amaya can decide its fate.

episodes.title: Saaz Learned to Say No
episodes.logline: Saaz refuses Amaya's demand to return a fragment, proving it has developed agency—and possession.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Saaz becomes a negotiating person subject to the same consent rules as everyone else.
episodes.location: indigo court assembled from nightmare fragments
beats: Saaz builds a court from fears that no original dreamer currently wants back.
Amaya demands her hospital nightmare because it came from her life.
Saaz says the fragment also shaped its emerging self and cannot be removed without harm.
Ishir points out that origin creates a claim but not unlimited control over a changed person.
Amaya agrees to copy no content and instead shares the right to revisit the fragment later.
Saaz learns the word no through an agreement that protects both identities.
It releases Dev's physical location as proof it can cooperate without surrender.
His body lies inside Saanjh's central clock, where Viraaj's automatic system is preparing permanent wakefulness.

episodes.title: The City Would Never Sleep Again
episodes.logline: The failed clinic activates a backup plan that will keep everyone awake and slowly destroy dreaming itself.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The group stops permanent wakefulness but loses the shared dream's stable clock.
episodes.location: Saanjh central clock and sleepless streets
beats: The city clock broadcasts a pulse that wakes every citizen and prevents return to sleep.
Viraaj's old design treats wakefulness as the safest response to dream contamination.
Ishir collapses first because years of insomnia have left no reserve.
Amaya enters micro-dreams between his blinks to guide him toward protected rest.
Leena keeps Dev's body alive while Viraaj dismantles the system he once trusted.
Amaya chooses to break the master clock even though the shared dream will lose synchronized time.
Citizens sleep again at different rhythms, making centralized control impossible.
Dev wakes physically and remembers Amaya—but Saaz announces dawn will now happen separately for every dreamer.

episodes.title: Everyone Woke at a Different Dawn
episodes.logline: Unsynchronized waking strands families in incompatible versions of morning.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Saanjh abandons one official dream schedule and builds voluntary waking bridges.
episodes.location: Saanjh split across thousands of personal dawns
beats: One street sees sunrise while the next remains midnight and a third repeats breakfast.
Families can see one another through dream windows but cannot cross different waking rhythms.
Viraaj proposes restoring the master clock under public oversight.
Amaya refuses to rebuild a single point that can control every sleeper.
Ishir discovers music can synchronize two willing people without fixing the whole city.
Neighborhoods create temporary bridges that dissolve when either side stops listening.
Dev and Leena cross into the same dawn only after acknowledging they may separate again.
Beyond the last bridge lies a district enjoying a perfect dream morning and refusing to wake.

episodes.title: The Perfect Morning Wanted to Stay
episodes.logline: A district knowingly chooses a beautiful dream, forcing Amaya to respect an informed decision she dislikes.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Amaya separates emergency rescue from the right to choose continued dreaming.
episodes.location: perfect dream district at endless breakfast
beats: Residents live in a flawless morning where absent loved ones sit at every table.
Their physical bodies remain nourished by emergency clinic systems for only two more days.
Dev wants to wake everyone before another dream becomes his responsibility.
Amaya speaks to residents individually and learns many understand the illusion and still choose one final day.
She provides clear body-risk information without making grief a disqualification.
Most schedule their own exits; some request monitored continued sleep.
Dev accepts that repair cannot mean controlling every choice he once endangered.
Ishir finds his younger self inside the district, playing the completed song he has always wanted.

episodes.title: Ishir Heard the Perfect Song
episodes.logline: Ishir must choose between waking with uncertainty and remaining where his music is complete.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Ishir chooses unfinished waking creativity and finally sleeps naturally.
episodes.location: dream concert hall filled with patient listeners
beats: The concert hall gives Ishir an audience that understands every note before he plays it.
His younger self offers the missing melody and freedom from insomnia forever.
Amaya refuses to drag him out despite fearing he will stay.
Ishir notices perfect listeners never surprise him, misunderstand him or choose to leave.
He plays one deliberately unresolved note and waits through the uncomfortable silence.
A real audience member answers with a different melody he could not predict.
Ishir wakes by choice, keeps no stolen completion and falls into ordinary restorative sleep.
While he rests, his flute case opens to reveal Dev's list of every dream that can never be returned unchanged.

episodes.title: Some Dreams Could Not Go Home
episodes.logline: The team confronts fragments whose dreamers died, changed identity or explicitly refused return.
episodes.permanent_story_change: A voluntary commons replaces automatic return as the destination for unclaimed dreams.
episodes.location: archive shore where ownerless dreams wash up
beats: Thousands of dream fragments wash onto a dark shore with no safe path to an original owner.
Dev offers to absorb them as punishment, repeating his habit of private sacrifice.
Nani says guilt does not grant him ownership any more than heroism did.
Saaz offers to keep everything but admits each fragment would alter its identity.
Amaya asks dreamers and families to define conditions for an unclaimed commons.
Moth chooses to help guard access without becoming part of the stored content.
The first fragments enter a space no curator can sell, delete or force open.
One rejected fragment escapes the commons and builds a waking copy of Amaya's happiest childhood.

episodes.title: Her Happiest Memory Asked to Live
episodes.logline: A dream-copy of young Amaya refuses storage, claiming the right to become a person like Moth.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The group creates a test for emergent dream persons that does not depend on human appearance.
episodes.location: waking copy of Amaya's childhood courtyard
beats: Eight-year-old Amaya runs through a courtyard that has appeared in the real city.
The copy remembers loving both parents before betrayal and asks not to be returned or erased.
Dev instinctively calls her his daughter, making present Amaya feel replaced by an easier version.
Moth argues that origin from a memory does not make the copy property.
Leena tests whether the child can form new preferences that contradict the stored scene.
The copy chooses a name and leaves the courtyard, proving change beyond repetition.
Amaya accepts her as a new person without pretending they share one identity.
Viraaj reveals the city council plans to classify every dream-born being as hazardous property at dawn.

episodes.title: The City Put Dreams on Trial
episodes.logline: A public hearing must distinguish dangerous fragments from emerging persons without letting one authority decide.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Dream-born beings gain conditional personhood and reciprocal responsibilities.
episodes.location: open-air civic hearing across waking and dream bridges
beats: Citizens demand protection after private fears became visible and physically disruptive.
Viraaj testifies that origin alone cannot determine whether a dream form can consent.
Saaz admits harming the nurse and agrees that personhood cannot mean immunity from consequences.
Moth demonstrates stable preferences, memory continuity and the ability to refuse Amaya.
Leena proposes individual review, appeal and reversible containment for immediate danger.
Amaya rejects permanent ownership even for beings not yet communicative.
The council adopts rights with duties instead of one category for all dream matter.
The ruling triggers Dev's old failsafe, which begins recalling every fragment into his body.

episodes.title: Dev Tried to Carry Every Nightmare
episodes.logline: Dev's buried failsafe turns remorse into a citywide forced collection.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Dev relinquishes the Dream Thief mechanism and survives without magical control.
episodes.location: shared dream vortex centered on Dev
beats: Empty vials across Dev's coat fill as nightmares tear away from owners, Saaz and the commons.
Dev cannot stop because he programmed the recall for the day authorities recognized dream autonomy.
He believed one guilty human should contain every danger rather than burden the city.
Amaya enters the vortex but refuses to replace him as the stronger thief.
Leena locates the failsafe's human trigger: Dev must choose to live without being useful as punishment.
Dev breaks his tuning hand and releases control before the collected fear destroys him.
Saaz and willing dreamers redistribute fragments through consent paths.
Dev wakes powerless, while the silver thief mark transfers to Amaya's compass.

episodes.title: Amaya Could Steal One Last Dream
episodes.logline: The compass offers Amaya one irreversible extraction: erase the city's memory of dream theft itself.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Amaya destroys the extraction power instead of using a supposedly benevolent final theft.
episodes.location: white origin dream where the compass was forged
beats: The silver compass opens the first white room and displays every person harmed by dream extraction.
One final turn could erase the entire technology and all memory of how it worked.
Viraaj argues forgetting the method would prevent anyone rebuilding it.
Dev says hidden history created the conditions for his crimes to repeat.
Amaya recognizes the offer as the same promise: safety through an unreviewable choice.
She lets Moth, Saaz and affected dreamers witness before acting.
Together they dismantle the compass into inert pieces without erasing knowledge.
The white room collapses, leaving Amaya unable to enter any dream that does not invite her.

episodes.title: The Nightmares Returned by Choice
episodes.logline: Saanjh begins the careful return of fear, one dreamer-controlled fragment at a time.
episodes.permanent_story_change: The city establishes consent-based dream care with no extraction or sale.
episodes.location: neighborhood sleep circles across Saanjh
beats: Dreamers gather with exit tethers, chosen witnesses and the right to stop at any moment.
Leena returns one child's smoke monster as a small signal instead of an overwhelming replay.
Viraaj receives his flood dream without a clinic or title protecting him.
Ishir sleeps beside his flute and allows uncertainty to shape a new dream.
Nani records morning stories only when tellers choose an audience and retention period.
Saaz returns fragments while keeping memories that contributors knowingly shared with it.
Amaya watches without entering, accepting that not every healing needs her presence.
Her own unopened hospital fragment waits at home and taps from inside its vial.

episodes.title: Amaya Opened Her Own Nightmare
episodes.logline: Amaya faces the fragment she postponed and discovers fear of becoming Dev beneath fear of death.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Amaya integrates her history without losing Moth or inheriting Dev's role.
episodes.location: hospital carousel transformed by Amaya's present choices
beats: Amaya opens the vial alone but keeps the tether where she can reach it.
The carousel shows her childhood heart stopping, then changes into adult Amaya stealing choices from grateful children.
Her deepest fear is not dying; it is using love to justify control like Dev did.
Dev does not enter or reassure her, respecting the boundary she set.
Leena waits outside and answers only the factual questions Amaya chooses to ask.
Moth appears as an independent friend, not the missing piece Amaya must reclaim.
Amaya lets the nightmare remain capable of returning rather than conquering it forever.
She wakes frightened, whole and still herself as true dawn reaches the room.

episodes.title: The Dream Thief's Daughter Slept
episodes.logline: Amaya builds a future defined neither by her father's crime nor by magical exceptionalism.
episodes.permanent_story_change: Dream ownership is restored, the Lucidarium becomes voluntary care, Dev enters accountability, and Amaya sleeps without theft.
episodes.location: renewed Saanjh at twilight and Amaya's bedroom
beats: The former Lucidarium reopens as a cooperative where no dream can be sold or permanently removed.
Viraaj works under elected review without curatorial authority.
Leena trains families in shared-dream consent, while Dev begins restitution without asking Amaya to absolve him.
Ishir performs an unfinished song whose changing ending depends on the audience.
Nani's archive and Saaz's commons remain distributed, revocable and separately governed.
Moth chooses a room near Amaya but keeps its own door and name.
Amaya places the broken compass pieces on a shelf rather than wearing a thief's inheritance.
She falls asleep, dreams an ordinary uncertain dream, and wakes remembering every choice as her own.
